```{r setup}
# Render AFTER source("run_all.R"); this report only reads results/.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(tidyverse); library(knitr) })
tb  <- function(f) read_csv(file.path("results/tables", f), show_col_types = FALSE)
fig <- function(f) knitr::include_graphics(file.path("results/figures", f))
de_sum <- tb("DE_summary.csv")
mag    <- tb("region_effect_magnitude.csv")
comp   <- tb("ED_composition_check.csv")
n_of   <- function(a, col = "DEG") de_sum[[col]][de_sum$analysis == a]
```

## Design

Same-length (elongated, short) day-15 conceptuses; ED and TE sections taken from **the same embryo**.

```{r}
read_csv("metadata/samples.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(same_length) %>% select(sample, embryo, type, region, section, cryopreserved) %>% kable()
```

* Primary comparison: IVP vs IVV within each region, 4 vs 4 embryos (IVPF10_EC, the only fresh IVP library, excluded).
* **Confounding:** every IVP embryo is male and every IVV embryo female, and each group comes from two dams,
  so "IVP effect" here means *IVP + sex + dam*. These cannot be separated with these samples.

## Quality control

```{r}
fig("qc_pca_same_length.png")
```

```{r}
tb("qc_within_group_correlation.csv") %>% head(6) %>% kable(digits = 3,
  caption = "Lowest mean correlation with libraries of the same region and type")
```

IVP9_T1A correlates noticeably less with the other TE libraries than any other library does;
IVP9 is also the only embryo sectioned at position "A" rather than "C". TE results are therefore also
reported without IVP9_T1A (sensitivity analysis).

### Disc content of ED sections

```{r}
fig("qc_disc_score_ED.png")
```

Disc-enriched genes were defined from the IVV embryos alone (ED vs TE of the same embryo). Several IVP ED
sections (IVP10_EC, IVP11_EC and the excluded IVPF10_EC) express these genes at clearly lower levels than any
IVV ED section. Either the IVP discs are smaller or less developed (biologically plausible for IVP
conceptuses), or the sections contain more trophectoderm. Either way, part of the "down in IVP ED"
signal reflects **tissue composition** rather than lower expression per disc cell (see below).

## Differential expression (IVP vs IVV)

```{r}
de_sum %>% kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r}
fig("volcano_MA_ED_IVP_vs_IVV.png"); fig("volcano_MA_TE_IVP_vs_IVV.png")
```

### How much of the ED result is composition?

```{r}
comp %>% kable(digits = 2)
```

Across ED DEGs, the IVP-vs-IVV fold change correlates negatively with how disc-specific the gene is in
IVV embryos (Spearman rho = `r round(comp$spearman_rho_all_DEG[1], 2)`). Adjusting the ED model for
the disc-content score leaves `r n_of("ED_disc_adjusted")` DEGs (from `r n_of("ED")`). Because disc content
itself differs between groups, the adjusted model is conservative: it may also remove real IVP effects.
Both versions should be reported.

## Is one region more affected than the other?

```{r}
mag %>% pivot_longer(everything()) %>% kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r}
fig("IVPeffect_ED_vs_TE_scatter.png")
```

The correct test for "does IVP affect TE and ED differently" is the region × treatment interaction in a
model that uses the ED/TE pairing within embryos (`03_joint_model.R`). It identified
`r mag$interaction_genes_FDR05` genes at FDR < 0.05, and the IVP effects in the two regions are
positively correlated (r = `r round(mag$pearson_r_IVPeffect_ED_vs_TE, 2)`). ED has more DEGs
(`r mag$DEG_ED` vs `r mag$DEG_TE`), partly because of the composition shift described above.

## Functional enrichment

ORA used up- and down-regulated DEGs separately against the background of tested genes (BH FDR).
GSEA used all tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic.

```{r}
#| results: asis
for (f in c("GO_compareCluster_ED_TE.png",
            "GSEA_dotplot_ED_IVP_vs_IVV.png", "GSEA_dotplot_TE_IVP_vs_IVV.png",
            "GSEA_dotplot_ED_IVP_vs_IVV_discAdjusted.png")) {
  if (file.exists(file.path("results/figures", f))) cat(sprintf("![](results/figures/%s)\n\n", f))
}
```

## Classifier sanity check (optional)

```{r}
if (file.exists("results/tables/classifier_loeo_summary.csv")) {
  tb("classifier_loeo_summary.csv") %>% kable(digits = 3)
}
```

Leave-one-embryo-out CV with feature selection inside each fold, compared against all 70 embryo-level
label permutations. With 8 embryos this is a coarse check only.

### IVP vs IVV from one region, and across regions

```{r}
if (file.exists("results/tables/classifier_by_region_summary.csv")) {
  tb("classifier_by_region_summary.csv") %>%
    select(analysis, n_features, accuracy_svm, p_svm, accuracy_rf, p_rf,
           rf_mean_prob_true_class, p_rf_prob) %>% kable(digits = 3)
}
```

```{r}
if (file.exists("results/figures/classifier_by_region.png")) fig("classifier_by_region.png")
```

Within-region accuracy shows whether one region alone identifies the procedure. Cross-region transfer
(train on TE, predict ED and vice versa) shows whether the IVP signature is shared (high accuracy),
region-specific (about 0.5) or inverted (below 0.5). With 8 embryos, the smallest attainable permutation
p-value is 2/70 = 0.029.
